circuits.notes: PUBLISHED FOR EARLY TESTING ONLY: this circuit is unreviewed, AI-generated code. The crate's planned expert security review (sha256_var/mso_splice/onehot_cursor/digest_id_extract, plus a known ECDSA range-check gap) has not landed. Do not treat as vouched-for or production-ready; do not rely on it for real relying-party trust decisions. | Supersedes r10: independent human review flagged that ClaimDigestStepCircuit::public_values exposed an undisclosed claim's raw SHA-256 digest publicly regardless of disclosure - a real cross-presentation correlation leak. Both circuits now expose SHA256(digest || nonce) instead (nonce fresh per presentation); the step<->core binding check moved from reconstructing the real MSO z from raw digests to a direct per-slot blinded-digest comparison, which also let the previously-exposed z itself stop being public (it was also a stable per-credential value). Also enables LTO for release builds (~5% perf) and widens MAX_VAR_MESSAGE_BYTES 128->176 for a real 136-byte PID claim seen in live testing. This changes the circuit's constraint wiring and public-value shape, so r10 keys/proofs are not interchangeable with r11's.

source.toolchain: microsoft/vega-prover rev c0ee259, zk-cred-vega setup() (sirosfoundation/zk-cred-vega v0.0.1)

circuits.notes: PUBLISHED FOR EARLY TESTING ONLY: this circuit is unreviewed, AI-generated code. The crate's planned expert security review (sha256_var/mso_splice/onehot_cursor/digest_id_extract, plus a known ECDSA range-check gap) has not landed. Do not treat as vouched-for or production-ready; do not rely on it for real relying-party trust decisions. | Fixes a real under-constraint found while scoping that review: digest_id_extract's value-byte mapping is right-aligned, so for CBOR uint length classes 0/1/2 the high-order bytes of the exposed digestID were free witness variables, and both range checks went vacuous (gated by a different class's selector). A prover generating its own witness could select class 1 to match real bytes 0x18 0x1A (digestID 26) while exposing 0x0ABBCC1A -- defeating the digestID-to-claim-bytes binding r6 was meant to establish. Fixed by constraining every value byte the selected class does not encode to zero, per-class, with a regression test that tampers with the witness directly (verified to fail without the fix). Likely fail-safe rather than forgeable (a conformant verifier rejects), but it broke the intended guarantee. Supersedes r6 (deprecated). | publish: cleanup: consolidate note text | deprecated: Superseded by r8: MAX_VAR_MESSAGE_BYTES widened 128->176 (a real PID mdoc's IssuerSignedItemBytes at 136 bytes exceeded r7's budget).
